item.title: Sequels Keep Getting Bigger, But This New Survival Horror Game Got Better by Being Smaller
item.description:
Creating a worthy sequel is hard. The first game sets certain expectations, and many developers fall into the common trend of making sure the second chapter is bigger in nearly every single way. That's not really a bad thing, of course, but The Sinking City 2 has proven that a sequel can actually succeed at being a better game while also being much smaller. The Sinking City 2 completely turns away from the foundation its predecessor laid, and it's better off for it.

It's been seven years since the first Sinking City was released. Developer Frogwares' Lovecraftian mystery had plenty of interesting concepts, but the game didn't quite deliver on what it could have been, making for some heavily mixed reviews. However, Frogwares went back to the drawing board with the sequel, and the new direction has made feedback to The Sinking City 2 far more positive. There are several key reasons why The Sinking City 2 is a stronger experience than its predecessor, but the core game-changer is that Frogwares scaled back the game's overall scope.

New Survival Horror Game on Steam is Division Meets Fallout with a Unique Jurassic Park Twist

A new survival horror title on Steam merges The Division’s secret agent vibe with Fallout’s scavenging, all while adding dinosaurs to the mix.

By Richard Warren

The Sinking City 2 Is a Great Demonstration of How Sequels Don't Always Have to Go Bigger to Be Great

Whether it's a video game, a movie, or even a book, sequels tend to expand the lore and world by going bigger. It only makes sense, but that approach simply doesn't work for every kind of story. Going bigger sometimes risks losing sight of what made a story so compelling in the first place. What's so interesting is that The Sinking City 's story actually started off too big.

The first game featured an open-world investigation formula, and even though it worked in some instances, it often made the experience feel more repetitive and tedious over time. This time around, Frogwares decided to opt for a linear survival horror story akin to games like Resident Evil Requiem and Alan Wake 2 . Fans of the first Sinking City who loved the investigative elements will still be able to scratch that detective fantasy itch with this sequel, but it will just be within a more tight-knit world design and isn't as central to the plot.

Games With Sequels That Went Bigger Than the Previous Chapter

  • Horizon Zero Dawn Horizon Forbidden West
  • Red Dead Redemption Red Dead Redemption 2
  • The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
  • The Witcher 2: Assassins of Kings The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt
  • Batman: Arkham Origins Batman: Arkham Knight

The games listed above make it clear that going bigger with a sequel often works incredibly well. Expanding a game with every new entry can be a great way to make in-game exploration more exciting. It's just that Frogwares realized that that kind of approach wouldn't work for The Sinking City 2 . The first game's open-world design held it back, and Frogwares' decision to rein in the sequel was a risky leap into the unknown that ended up being the foundation of a much better iteration of a Lovecraftian world. Games inspired by Lovecraft are all about the atmosphere, and a survival horror formula is a much stronger genre to bring that kind of cosmic dread to life.

The Sinking City 2 Is Resident Evil and Silent Hill Wrapped Up in a Cosmic Nightmare

Because of its pivot into the survival horror genre, a lot of reviews have been comparing The Sinking City 2 to the Resident Evil and Silent Hill games. Resident Evil 's resource scarcity is a defining feature of the franchise, while Silent Hill is focused heavily on psychological torment and dread. The Sinking City 2 combines both of these, and it enhances the game's bleak atmosphere.

Frogwares' decision to rein in the sequel was a risky leap into the unknown that ended up being the foundation of a much better iteration of a Lovecraftian world.

Protagonist Calvin Raffery has to investigate the town of Arkham's mysterious flood that harbors disgusting water-dwelling parasites called the Slither. These stomach-churning hive mind slugs take over the bodies of corpses, giving rise to one of the scariest body horror monsters of 2026. The Slither requires players to be strategic and careful when being dealt with, and these moments are when the Resident Evil and Silent Hill influences become quite clear. GamesRadar's review had some compelling points about this combo:

Plenty of moments throughout The Sinking City 2 , ammo and health feel scarce enough to the point I have to seriously consider which enemies are worth blasting out of my way or simply trying to dodge my way around. Because, even when felled, The Slither can keep coming. Even now, I don't fully understand how this works, but the wormy abominations that burst forth from a defeated enemy can dart across to a new corpse to animate, making some areas feel like slaughterhouses with how many Slither keep coming.

The Slither creates a sense of helplessness that is essential for any great survival horror game. It's completely possible for open-world games to be scary, but The Sinky City 2 showcases how much more effective the survival horror genre is at creating such a deep and sweat-inducing helpless feeling. The linear design makes you feel cornered and claustrophobic, which is needed in order to make the Slither feel like a true threat.

Frogwares Didn't Have to Change The Sinking City 2's Formula, But This Decision Probably Saved the Game

As a developer, it can't be easy deciding to tone down the original vision's scope. However, Frogwares wanted to tell a scarier story and understood that this required a significant rework. There are plenty of game sequels that are better than the original, but that isn't an easy thing to achieve.

The Case for and Against Bloober’s Silent Hill Remake Being Longer Than the Original
Why Weapons Director Zach Cregger is the Perfect Pick for the New Resident Evil Movie
Resident Evil Requiem Ending Explained
40 Years Later, Zelda Still Hasn't Topped Its Greatest Surprise

Frogwares took a risk that has made The Sinking City 2 one of the most intriguing horror games of 2026. After the success of Resident Evil Requiem and the upcoming Silent Hill: Townfall release at the end of September, it's going to be fascinating to see how this dread-filled Lovecraftian mystery stacks up against these larger horror franchise entries.

The Sinking City 2

item.title: Xbox Officially Makes 3 Games 100% Free for a Limited Time
item.description:
Xbox is giving gamers another opportunity to play games for free, with three titles that have been made available through the weekend for Xbox Game Pass subscribers. The games will be available from August 20 through August 23, and all three standard tiers of Xbox Game Pass subscribers are eligible for the offer.

For new Xbox Game Pass subscribers and those who have never taken advantage of the offer before, gaining access to the three Xbox titles is easy. Players can simply access the subscriptions tab of the Xbox Store and scroll until they see Free Play Days, where this weekend's titles are listed.

Xbox Reveals Unexpected Collaboration

Xbox officially shows off a new collaboration, and it's with a company most fans probably would not expect them to partner with.

By Marc Deschamps

Xbox Free Play Days Game List (August 20-23)

The free games offered via Xbox Free Play Days from August 20 through August 23 are Train Sim World 6 , Icarus: Console Edition , and Lynked: Banner of the Spark . Gamers who have friends who also subscribe to Xbox Game Pass Ultimate, Premium, or Essential can play Icarus: Console Edition and Lynked: Banner of the Spark together, adding to the potential fun. Details on the Free Weekend promo and each game follow, plus links to their store listings.

  • Train Sim World 6: Standard Edition
  • ICARUS: Console Edition
  • Lynked: Banner of the Spark

Free Xbox Play Days Game: Train Sim World 6

Train Sim World 6 is the latest annual iteration in train simulator games from Dovetail Games. The base edition of the game adds three new transit networks, including New Jersey Transit's Morristown Line, England's Riviera Line, and Germany's Bahnstrecke Leipzig-Dresden. Train types like the Arrow III EMU, "Intercity" Class 802, and ICE-T have been made available, respectively, and train enthusiast gamers have a wide range of options to explore and try out.

  • Release Date : September 30, 2025
  • Genre : Simulation
  • Developer : Dovetail Games
  • Publisher : Dovetail Games
  • Metascore : N/A for Xbox, 76 for PC (Generally Favorable)
  • Can you beat it before the Free Play Days Promotion ends? As a sim game, it has no standard ending.
  • Current price : $49.99
  • Xbox Store Link: Play Train Sim World 6 for Free on Xbox

Free Xbox Play Days Game: ICARUS: Console Edition

Icarus: Console Edition drops up to four players onto a terraform-failed planet filled with dangers, ranging from the frontier itself to wild creatures to fend against. Players have to work together to create a shelter and hunt for food, all while dealing with harsh weather like lightning storms. The game notably comes from the creator of DayZ , one of the best-known open-world zombie survival games around.

  • Genre : Survival
  • Developer : GRIP Studios
  • Publisher : GRIP Studios
  • Metascore : N/A for Xbox, 67 for PC (Mixed or Average)
  • Can you beat it before the Free Play Days Promotion ends? The main story can be completed in about 36 hours, which isn't impossible, but difficult over a single weekend.
  • Current price : $39.99
  • Xbox Store Link: Play Icarus: Console Edition for Free on Xbox
Xbox Officially Makes 3 Games 100% Free for a Limited Time
Pokemon FireRed and LeafGreen Players Can Get Free Celebi
Steam Officially Makes 2 Games 100% Free Until August 24, Includes 200-Player Multiplayer Game
Riot Game Development Permanently Shutting Down in December 2026

Free Xbox Play Days Game: Lynked: Banner of the Spark

Lynked: Banner of the Spark is a game where 1 to 3 players can band together with robots called Unibots assisting them. The game is described as a cross between an action roguelite and a life sim, with combat against swarms of enemy robots, whose parts can then be used for base-building. Players can go fishing, farming, and more. The game features over 80 variations of 10 unique weapon classes, character customization, and Unibots can be upgraded to assist in fights.

  • Release Date: May 22, 2025
  • Genre: Action Adventure
  • Developer : FuzzyBot
  • Publisher : Dreamhaven
  • Metascore : N/A for Xbox, 83 for PS5 (Generally Favorable)
  • Can you beat it before the Free Play Days Promotion ends? No.
  • Current price : $14.99
  • Xbox Store Link: Play Lynked: Banner of the Spark for Free on Xbox

Source: Xbox Wire

item.title: 7 Long Tactical RPGs That Take Forever to Complete, Ranked
item.description:
With Star Wars Zero Company and Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave both on the way, I've had tactical RPGs on the brain quite a bit lately, and naturally, that also means thinking about just how much time these games can take up. That's not necessarily a bad thing, either. In fact, I'd argue that's part of what makes the genre such an easy buy for an RPG fan like myself. It's already hard enough to put one of these games down when there are generally so many different story routes to take or character builds to try, but when all of that is packed into a game that can take well over 100 hours to fully complete, suddenly you've got something that can keep you busy for a very long time.

And there are some tactical RPGs that take that idea much further than others. Plenty of them can last 40 or 50 hours and already feel like a pretty big commitment, but that's almost nothing compared to the games that can double, triple, or even quadruple that number if you want to see everything they have to offer. Some of them get there through a choice-driven story with multiple outcomes, while others simply have so much optional content and progression to dig into that finishing the main story barely feels like finishing the game at all. So, with Star Wars Zero Company and Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave giving tactical RPG fans like myself plenty to look forward to, there's arguably no better time to look at some of the genre's biggest time sinks.

The tactical RPGs on this list are ranked by their estimated overall completion time according to HowLongToBeat, though individual playtimes can vary significantly.

7 Triangle Strategy

One Playthrough Only Tells Part of the Story

  • Check out Triangle Strategy on Steam
  • HowLongToBeat average length: 34.5 hours main / 104 hours completionist

At first glance, Triangle Strategy doesn't seem quite as intimidating as some of the other games on this list, especially since its main story takes around 34.5 hours to finish on average . That's still a decent chunk of time, of course, but it's also nowhere near the kind of commitment you'd expect from a tactical RPG that can eventually take more than 100 hours to fully complete. The catch is that Triangle Strategy isn't really built around seeing everything in one playthrough. Its story regularly asks you to make decisions that can send things in entirely different directions, sometimes changing the battles you'll fight and even where the story goes next. So, getting to the credits once is really only seeing one version of how everything can play out.

11 Best Tactical RPGs With Deep Character Customization, Ranked

Those who love to customize their characters to be just the way they like are in for something special in these tactical RPGs.

By Mark Sammut

That's where Triangle Strategy 's 104-hour completionist average starts making a lot more sense, because seeing everything means going back and making choices you intentionally avoided the first time around. There are different endings to reach, characters you may not have recruited, and entire stretches of the story that can be missed depending on the decisions your group makes. Thankfully, New Game Plus makes going through it again a little easier, but you're still looking at multiple playthroughs if you actually want to squeeze everything out of it. A 34.5-hour tactical RPG might not sound too outrageous, but Triangle Strategy has a way of turning one campaign into several before you're truly done with it.

6 Brigandine: The Legend of Runersia

Conquering an Entire Continent Is No Small Commitment

  • Check out Brigandine: The Legend of Runersia on Steam
  • HowLongToBeat average length: 27 hours main / 127 hours completionist

Brigandine: The Legend of Runersia is another one of those games where the main story doesn't really tell the whole story. According to HowLongToBeat, you can make it through a single campaign in around 27 hours , which actually makes it one of the shorter games on this list if that's all you're looking at. But Brigandine is built around choosing one of six different nations and trying to conquer the entire continent of Runersia with that faction, so finishing it once naturally leaves quite a bit on the table. Each nation has its own ruler and story, and while the overall goal stays the same, going back through the game with another faction gives you a different starting point and another side of the conflict to see.

That's a big reason why Brigandine: The Legend of Runersia jumps all the way up to a 127-hour completionist average , because actually seeing everything means doing a lot more than conquering Runersia once and calling it a day. There's also its Challenge Mode to dig into, which lets you put together a more customized army and gives you another reason to keep playing after you've already spent dozens of hours with the main campaigns. So, while 27 hours might not sound all that bad for a tactical RPG, that's really only if you're satisfied with seeing one nation's story through to the end. If you're the kind of player who wants to see what everyone else was up to while you were busy taking over the continent, Brigandine can suddenly become a much bigger commitment.

5 Wartales

Its Mercenary Adventure Can Consume Entire Weeks

  • Check out Wartales on Steam
  • HowLongToBeat average length: 42 hours main / 146 hours completionist

Wartales is already a fairly long tactical RPG if all you want to do is work your way through its main content, with HowLongToBeat putting that at around 42 hours on average . But with a game like this, I almost feel like that number doesn't tell you much, because Wartales isn't really the kind of game where you just keep your head down and push toward the finish line. In this game, it feels like you're constantly finding something else that needs your attention, so even if you go into it thinking you're going to stick to the important stuff, it's very easy for that plan to fall apart. And really, that's where a lot of the appeal is, because so much of Wartales is built around everything that happens in between whatever you might consider its main objectives.

That becomes even more obvious once you look at its 146-hour completionist average , which is more than three times what it takes to simply get through the main content. That's a massive difference, but it also makes sense for a game that gives you so many reasons to keep wandering off and doing something else. You might head somewhere with one goal in mind, only to end up spending hours taking on contracts, improving your mercenaries, or dealing with whatever you happened to find along the way instead. So while 42 hours is already nothing to scoff at, anyone who gets hooked on the part of Wartales that exists outside that most direct path can very easily find themselves spending well over 100 hours with it before they're ready to move on.

4 Tactics Ogre: Reborn

Finishing the Story Is Only the Beginning

  • Check out Tactics Ogre: Reborn on Steam
  • HowLongToBeat average length: 54 hours main / 176 hours completionist

Tactics Ogre: Reborn is where the time commitment on this list starts getting a little more serious, because even just getting through its main story takes around 54 hours on average, according to HowLongToBeat. That's already longer than plenty of RPGs take to finish altogether, but the problem with Tactics Ogre is that seeing the credits once doesn't necessarily mean you've seen anywhere close to everything. The story can branch in different directions based on the decisions you make, which means one playthrough is naturally going to leave some things behind. item.title: Pokemon FireRed and LeafGreen Players Can Get Free Celebi
item.description:
Pokemon FireRed and LeafGreen players will officially be able to get Celebi for free very soon. Pokemon FireRed and LeafGreen came out as Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 ports on Pokemon Day 2026, and they quickly became some of the most successful titles sold on the official Nintendo Store, often claiming first and second place on the sales charts, respectively. Ever since the ports came out, though, players have been asking about Pokemon Home support, as the Pokedex cannot be completed natively within the ports.

This is because Pokemon FireRed and LeafGreen would actually need Gen 3 games to complete the National Pokedex via trading, as some Pokemon cannot be found in either title regardless of version exclusivity. Now, Pokemon FireRed and LeafGreen 's Home compatibility is finally coming in October 2026, as announced recently, and this is great news for players on multiple fronts. Not only will players be able to transfer Pokemon caught in FRLG , but they will also be able to complete their Home Pokedex with them simply by registering them in-game — no transfer needed. On top of that, fans will also get Celebi entirely for free.

Pokemon FireRed and LeafGreen on Switch Include Legendary and Mythical Event Pokemon

Pokemon FireRed and LeafGreen on Switch have access to some Legendary and Mythical event Pokemon, perhaps surprising some fans.

By Joshua Duckworth

You Can Now Officially Get Celebi Thanks to Pokemon FireRed and LeafGreen

When Home support launches, Pokemon FireRed and LeafGreen players will be able to complete their Pokedex in Pokemon Home simply by registering critters in the Switch ports, which will unlock Celebi in Pokemon Home for free. Currently, there is no way to get Celebi in Pokemon FireRed and LeafGreen natively, and unfortunately, this will not change with Home support. In fact, The Pokemon Company confirmed that fans won't be able to transfer Pokemon into FRLG , but only from the ports. As such, the National Pokedex issue remains, despite the addition of a free Celebi within Pokemon Home for completing the Pokedex.

These games are needed to finish the National Pokedex in Pokemon FireRed and LeafGreen , so launching them alongside Pokemon Home compatibility is a smart move. Before Home support was even confirmed for October 2026, the Gen 3 ports were also leaked to be planned for the same month. This makes sense because Celebi may be one of the few Pokemon that won't be obtainable for Pokemon FRLG 's National Pokedex even after Home support launches, so giving it away for free in the mobile app for Pokemon Home is a perfect way to handle it.

Approach the IPSF checkpoint, the entrance to the Iron Forest base, after defeating some mutants.

Duty Route : Speak to Lieutenant Blatin after capturing the Water Purification Facility.

Freedom Route : Speak to Ihor Fox after defending the Water Purification Facility from Duty.

Duty Route : Speak to Sgt. Kamenetskyi at the Water Purification Facility in CNPP after completing Gunpowder, Sweat, and Blood main mission.

Fair Deal

Complete the Price of a Miracle main mission.

Territorial War

Duty Route : After receiving a call from Zulu after the Price of a Miracle main mission.

Freedom Route : After receiving a call from Zen after the Price of a Miracle main mission

Stalker 2: Cost of Hope is the first major story expansion that takes players to some of the most iconic locations in the Zone, including the Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant (CNPP). The DLC features several new main and side missions that will add roughly 15 to 20 hours of fresh content to the game. This guide will list all the main and side quests you can expect to complete in Stalker 2: Cost of Hope DLC.
